_loader_notes: Machine guides (AGENTS.md W4). Shown as 'First time on the [machine]?' in the cardio player and exercise info, and in Learn (Gym confidence).
Cardio machines are equipment for Gym unlocked (first-treadmill, first-bike, first-cross-trainer, first-rower, first-stair-climber badges).
Strength machine 'exercises' lists the catalogue exercises done on it, for 'Exercises you can do on this' (and later AI1 machine scan).
Exercise-specific setup and form cues live in the exercise guides; these cover the machine itself.
Draft for coach review before launch.
visual_features is a short look-for line for AI1 machine scan. Edit here; the Edge Function copies id, name and visual_features.

machines.name: Treadmill
machines.visual_features: Moving walking belt with side rails, a front console, and a clip-on safety key.
machines.where_to_find: In the cardio area, usually in rows facing windows or screens.
setup: Clip the safety key to your clothing before you start. If you slip, it pulls out and the belt stops.
Stand on the side rails, not the belt, while you press Start or Quick Start.
start_and_stop: Press Start and let the belt begin slowly. Step on once it's moving at walking pace.
Change speed and incline with the arrows or quick-select buttons.
To stop, lower the speed first, then press Stop. Step onto the side rails once the belt slows right down.
In an emergency, pull the safety key or press the red stop button.
machines.beginner_settings: Walking: 4 to 5.5 km/h. Incline: 0 to 6% to start. A 1% incline feels closest to walking outdoors.
common_mistakes: Holding the handrails on a steep incline. Lower the incline instead.
Stepping off a moving belt. Always slow down and stop first.
etiquette: Many gyms have a time limit when busy, often 20 to 30 minutes.
Wipe down the handrails and screen when you finish.

machines.name: Exercise bike
machines.visual_features: Upright or recumbent cycle with pedals, a saddle, and a small console.
machines.where_to_find: In the cardio area. Upright bikes look like a road bike; recumbent bikes have a seat with a backrest.
setup: Stand next to the bike and set the seat level with your hip bone.
Sit on and check: at the bottom of the pedal stroke, your knee should be slightly bent.
Slide your feet into the pedal straps so the ball of your foot is over the pedal.
start_and_stop: Most bikes start when you begin pedalling.
Use the plus and minus buttons to change resistance.
To finish, lower the resistance and pedal easily for a minute or two before getting off.
machines.beginner_settings: Cadence: 70 to 85 rpm. Resistance: low enough to pedal smoothly, high enough that you're not spinning freely.
common_mistakes: Seat too low, which can strain your knees.
Rocking side to side. Lower the resistance or the seat slightly.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handlebars after use.

machines.name: Cross-trainer
machines.visual_features: Standing elliptical with two long moving handles and foot pedals on rails. Also called an elliptical.
machines.where_to_find: In the cardio area. Also called an elliptical.
setup: Hold the fixed handles and step onto the foot pedals one at a time.
Feet in the middle of the pedals, heels down.
start_and_stop: Start pedalling forwards and the screen will wake up.
Hold the moving handles to use your arms, or the fixed ones for balance.
To stop, slow down gradually. Wait until the pedals stop before stepping off.
machines.beginner_settings: Resistance: low to moderate. Aim for a smooth, steady pace you could keep for 10 minutes or more.
common_mistakes: Leaning on the handles. Stand tall over your feet.
Up on your toes. Keep your heels down.
etiquette: Wipe down handles and pedals when you finish.

machines.name: Rowing machine
machines.visual_features: Long rail with a sliding seat, a fan housing, and a pull handle on a chain or strap.
machines.where_to_find: In the cardio or functional area, often on the floor near the walls.
setup: Sit on the seat and strap your feet in so the strap crosses the widest part of your foot.
Set the damper (the lever on the fan) to 3 to 5. Higher isn't better; it just feels heavier.
start_and_stop: The screen wakes up when you start rowing.
The stroke: push with your legs, lean back slightly, then pull the handle to your lower ribs. Return in reverse: arms, body, then legs.
To stop, row easily for a few strokes, then rest the handle in its holder.
machines.beginner_settings: Damper 3 to 5. 20 to 24 strokes a minute. Smooth and long beats fast and short.
common_mistakes: Pulling with your arms first. Legs do most of the work.
Rushing forward on the return. Take about twice as long coming forward as pushing back.
etiquette: Put the handle back gently. Don't let it fly back into the fan.
Wipe down the handle and seat.

machines.name: Stair climber
machines.visual_features: Small moving staircase with two handrails and a console.
machines.where_to_find: In the cardio area. It looks like a small moving staircase.
setup: Step onto the bottom stair while holding the rails.
Choose a low level before you start.
start_and_stop: Press Start and begin climbing as the stairs move.
Change speed with the plus and minus buttons.
To stop, press Stop and keep stepping until the stairs come to a halt. Step off carefully at the bottom.
machines.beginner_settings: Start low (about 3 to 5 on most machines) for 5 to 10 minutes. It's harder than it looks.
common_mistakes: Leaning heavily on the rails. Hold them lightly, just for balance.
Taking tiny steps on the edge. Use the whole step.
etiquette: Often busy, so keep to the gym's time limit.
Wipe down the rails.

machines.name: Leg press
machines.visual_features: Angled sled with a large footplate, a seat, and two safety handles.
machines.where_to_find: In the machine area, often near other leg machines. Look for a big angled sled with a seat and a footplate.
setup: Sit back with your back and head against the pad.
Feet hip-width on the middle of the footplate.
Add weight plates to the pegs on each side, or set the pin on a stack version.
how_to_use: Push the plate up slightly and turn the safety handles out to release it.
Lower until your knees are comfortably bent, then push back up.
When you finish, push up, turn the handles back in to lock it, then lower onto them.
machines.beginner_settings: Start with just the sled or one small plate each side. Add plates evenly to both sides.
common_mistakes: Locking your knees straight at the top.
Lowering so far that your lower back peels off the pad.
etiquette: It's fine to ask "How many sets have you got left?" or "Can I jump in between your sets?"
Take all the plates off when you're done.
Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Cable machine
machines.visual_features: Tall frame with one or two weight stacks, adjustable pulleys, and clip-on handles.
machines.where_to_find: Usually a tall frame with one or two weight stacks and adjustable pulleys, in the machine or functional area.
setup: Slide the pulley up or down the column by pulling the pin and moving it to the height you need.
Clip on the handle you need (rope, single handle, bar or ankle strap). They're usually hanging on the frame.
Choose the weight by putting the pin in the stack.
how_to_use: Step back so the weight lifts slightly off the stack at the start.
Move smoothly and don't let the weight slam down between reps.
machines.beginner_settings: Start very light. Cable weights feel heavier than the number suggests, especially with one arm.
common_mistakes: Letting the stack crash down. Control the return.
Standing too close, so the weight touches down every rep.
etiquette: Put the handle back where you found it.
It's fine to ask "How many sets have you got left?" or "Can I jump in between your sets?"

machines.name: Smith machine
machines.visual_features: Barbell fixed on vertical rails with hooks and safety stops, unlike a free squat rack.
machines.where_to_find: Looks like a squat rack with a barbell fixed on rails, usually near the free weights.
setup: Set the safety stops just below the lowest point you'll reach.
Position the bar at about shoulder height for squats.
Add plates evenly to each side if you need more than the bar.
how_to_use: Step under the bar, rest it across your upper back and stand up.
Twist your wrists to unhook the bar from its hooks.
Finish by twisting the bar back onto a hook at any level.
machines.beginner_settings: The bar alone usually weighs less than a normal barbell, often 6 to 15 kg. Check the label or ask staff.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to set the safety stops.
Feet directly under the bar. Step them slightly forward for squats.
etiquette: Strip the plates after use.
Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Squat rack
machines.visual_features: Tall free-standing frame with J-hooks and safety arms. The barbell is not fixed to rails.
machines.where_to_find: In the free-weights area: a tall frame with hooks (J-hooks) and safety arms.
setup: Set the J-hooks so the bar sits at mid-chest height.
Set the safety arms just below the bottom of your squat.
An Olympic barbell weighs 20 kg; many gyms also have 15 kg bars. Use clips to hold the plates on.
how_to_use: Step under the bar, brace and stand up to lift it off the hooks.
Take two or three small steps back.
When you finish, walk forwards until the bar touches the uprights, then lower it onto the hooks.
machines.beginner_settings: Start with the empty bar while you learn. There's no need to add plates until the movement feels steady.
common_mistakes: Setting the hooks too high, so you go on tiptoes to unrack.
Skipping the safety arms.
etiquette: Racks are in demand. Have your plan ready and share if someone asks.
Strip your plates when you're done.

machines.name: Lat pulldown
machines.visual_features: Seat with thigh pads and a long bar hanging from a high cable.
machines.where_to_find: In the machine area: a seat with knee pads and a long bar hanging from a cable above.
setup: Adjust the knee pad so your thighs are held snugly.
Choose the weight with the pin.
how_to_use: Stand, grab the bar slightly wider than your shoulders, then sit down with it.
Pull the bar to your upper chest, leading with your elbows.
At the end of your set, stand up slowly with the bar to return it.
machines.beginner_settings: Start light, around 15 to 25 kg, and focus on feeling your back work.
common_mistakes: Leaning way back to swing the weight.
Pulling the bar behind your head.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.
It's fine to ask "How many sets have you got left?" or "Can I jump in between your sets?"

machines.name: Seated cable row
machines.visual_features: Low bench with footplates and a cable at foot height, often with a V-handle.
machines.where_to_find: Usually a low bench with footplates and a cable at foot height, near the lat pulldown.
setup: Sit with your feet on the footplates and knees slightly bent.
Clip on the handle you'd like (the V-handle is most common).
how_to_use: Sit tall and pull the handle to your stomach, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Let your arms straighten slowly without rounding forward.
machines.beginner_settings: Start light and keep your back still. Your arms and back do the work, not your hips.
common_mistakes: Rocking back and forth.
Shrugging your shoulders up.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Chest press machine
machines.visual_features: Seated stack machine with two handles at chest height that press forward.
machines.where_to_find: In the machine area, often near the shoulder press.
setup: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Choose the weight with the pin.
how_to_use: Press the handles forward until your arms are straight but not locked.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch across your chest.
machines.beginner_settings: Start at a weight you could press 15 times, then adjust.
common_mistakes: Seat too low, so you press upwards.
Letting your shoulders roll forward.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Shoulder press machine
machines.visual_features: Seated stack machine with two handles at shoulder height that press upward.
machines.where_to_find: In the machine area, often next to the chest press.
setup: Set the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Choose the weight with the pin.
how_to_use: Press the handles up until your arms are nearly straight.
Lower slowly back to shoulder height.
machines.beginner_settings: Start light: shoulders are smaller muscles than your legs and chest.
common_mistakes: Arching your back off the pad.
Locking your elbows hard at the top.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Pec deck and rear delt machine
machines.visual_features: Seated machine with vertical pads or arms that meet in front of the chest; often reverses for rear delts.
machines.where_to_find: In the machine area. The same machine usually does chest flyes (facing out) and rear delt flyes (facing the pad).
setup: For chest: sit facing away from the pad and set the handles so they start just behind your shoulders.
For rear delts: sit facing the pad and set the handles to the front position.
Adjust the seat so the handles are at shoulder height.
how_to_use: Move with your arms slightly bent and the movement slow.
Return under control rather than letting the weight pull you back.
machines.beginner_settings: Start light. These are small, isolation movements.
common_mistakes: Seat at the wrong height, so your shoulders hunch.
Bending and straightening your elbows as you go.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Leg extension
machines.visual_features: Seat with a padded bar in front of the shins that lifts as you straighten your legs.
machines.where_to_find: With the other leg machines: a seat with a padded bar in front of your shins.
setup: Line your knees up with the machine's pivot point (usually a coloured dot).
Set the pad so it rests on the front of your ankles.
Choose the weight with the pin.
how_to_use: Straighten your legs to lift the pad, pause, then lower slowly.
machines.beginner_settings: Start light and use a slow lowering. It's an easy machine to go heavier on than you need.
common_mistakes: Swinging the weight up.
Knees out of line with the pivot.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Leg curl (seated or lying)
machines.visual_features: Seated or lying machine with a pad above the heels that you curl toward you.
machines.where_to_find: With the other leg machines. Seated versions have a pad over your thighs; lying versions have you face down.
setup: Line your knees up with the pivot point.
Set the pad so it sits just above your heels.
For the seated version, lower the thigh pad so it holds your legs in place.
how_to_use: Bend your knees to curl the pad, pause, then return slowly.
machines.beginner_settings: Start light; your hamstrings may cramp if you go heavy too soon.
common_mistakes: Lifting your hips off the seat or bench.
Rushing the return.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Hip thrust machine
machines.visual_features: Back pad like a bench with a padded belt or bar across the hips.
machines.where_to_find: In the machine or glute area, if your gym has one. It has a back pad and a padded belt or bar over your hips.
setup: Sit with your upper back on the pad and the belt or pad across your hips.
Feet flat, about hip-width, so your shins are vertical at the top.
how_to_use: Drive through your heels to lift your hips until they're in line with your body.
Squeeze your glutes at the top, then lower under control.
machines.beginner_settings: Start with a weight you can lift 12 times with a pause at the top.
common_mistakes: Arching your lower back at the top.
Feet too far forward, so you feel it in your hamstrings.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Hip abduction and adduction machine
machines.visual_features: Seated machine with pads on the outside or inside of the knees for outer or inner thighs.
machines.where_to_find: With the leg machines. Often the same machine does outer thighs (abduction) and inner thighs (adduction).
setup: Set the pads to the inside or outside of your knees, depending on which you're doing.
Choose a starting position that's comfortable.
how_to_use: Press your knees out (or in) smoothly, pause, then return slowly.
machines.beginner_settings: Light to moderate weight with a pause works best.
common_mistakes: Bouncing or using momentum.
Starting with your legs stretched too wide.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Assisted pull-up machine
machines.visual_features: Tall frame with overhead handles and a knee pad or standing platform. More stack weight makes it easier.
machines.where_to_find: In the machine area: a tall frame with handles at the top and a knee pad or platform.
setup: Choose the assistance with the pin. Here, more weight makes it easier.
Step up and kneel or stand on the platform.
how_to_use: Hold the handles and pull your chest up towards them.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
machines.beginner_settings: Start with plenty of assistance, often 30 to 50 kg, and reduce it over time.
common_mistakes: Dropping down quickly.
Not using the full range.
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Hack squat
machines.visual_features: Angled sled with shoulder pads and a footplate. You squat under the pads.
machines.where_to_find: In the leg machine area: an angled sled with shoulder pads.
setup: Stand on the footplate with your back against the pad and shoulders under the pads.
Feet hip-width, in the middle of the plate.
Release the safety handles.
how_to_use: Squat down under control, then push back up.
Lock the safety handles back in place when you finish.
machines.beginner_settings: Start with the empty sled; it already has some weight.
common_mistakes: Heels lifting off the plate.
Forgetting to re-engage the safety handles.
etiquette: Strip the plates after use.
Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.

machines.name: Calf raise machine
machines.visual_features: Standing or seated machine with a step edge for the balls of the feet and shoulder or knee pads.
machines.where_to_find: With the leg machines. It may be standing or seated.
setup: Put the balls of your feet on the edge of the step, heels hanging off.
Set the shoulder or knee pads so they're snug.
how_to_use: Rise up onto your toes, pause, then lower slowly into a stretch.
machines.beginner_settings: Moderate weight, a pause at the top and a slow stretch at the bottom.
common_mistakes: Bouncing quickly.
Bending your knees to help (on the standing version).
etiquette: Wipe down the seat and handles when you finish.
